We need to consider strategic goals: Gain castles/strongholds. Stark currently controls castle-black (castle) and winterfell (castle). Those are both castles. Already has 2 castles. So supply 1 allows up to two armies: one size up to 3 units, another size up to 2. Currently we have units: castle-black has 2 units (footman+knight) -> that forms an army of size 2 (in castle-black). That's one army. The footman at white-harbor is a single unit not an army. So total armies: one (size 2). If we move footman to moat-cailin, we will have two armies each size 2 (or maybe one army size 2 (castle-black) and another unit alone size 1 (but alone not an army). That's within supply.

If we also consider moving ship from the-shivering-sea to the-narrow-sea. The ship at the-shivering-sea can move to the-narrow-sea (sea). The-narrow-sea currently has no units (I think). It has no owner. That would give us a ship in a sea area, possibly useful for future ship transport. No castle there.

Strategically, gaining moat-cailin castle seems good: adds third castle, moving us closer to 7. Also may open path to other areas like the-twins etc.

Now ensure supply: after move, we have units in castle-black (2 units), moat-cailin (1 footman). That's okay.

Return JSON with action "resolve_march" ? need to see expected schema.
